notes.overview: Fast, hilly 4.1 km lap; flowing over blind crests matters more than braking performance. The first half links together (uphill T1, the crest into T3, then the Esses), each corner's speed setting up the next. T7 is the slowest point and opens the long back straight; the 10A/10B chicane leads to the run under the bridge and down the hill through fast, intimidating T12 onto the front straight. The biggest lap-time exits are T7 and T10B.

corners.1: Fast uphill right with slight banking. It's about momentum: brake lightly, just to load the front, and focus on exit speed up the hill. If the rear slides on exit, catch it gently; don't lift fully. Track out around mid-track to set up T2.
corners.2: Mostly the run-up to T3. Finish rotating here so the car's left tyres sit flush with the T3 entry curb on the left before braking; you want minimal steering lock while braking.
corners.3: Blind, tighter than it appears, braked over a crest: the trickiest point of the lap. Keep the wheel straight while braking or it spins. Some inside curb tightens the line. Turn-in is difficult to read; set your own reference points as your pace builds.
corners.4: Long left leading directly out of T3, opening the Esses: arrive at the track edge and turn left over the curb. Next is a fast, flat downhill right: keep left after T4, turn in just after the left entry curb (not usable), and run over the right-hand apex curbs. Your speed here was set at T3.
corners.5: Run along the straight left curb that closes the Esses, straddling it, and turn in at its end. Enter as at T3: car flush with the right entry curb to widen the radius, brake straight, and turn only once off the brake. Avoid the exit curb: very rough, and not worth the risk for the time.
corners.6: Steeply banked right with plenty of grip. The time here is on entry, not exit, since T7 comes up quickly: come off the brakes early and smoothly to carry speed in, and only just reach full throttle by the exit.
corners.7: Slowest point and most important corner, leading onto the mile-long back straight. Brake straight out of T6; it's tighter than it appears, so turn in later than feels natural. Trail-brake without overslowing the entry, then throttle hard early while unwinding the steering.
corners.8: Long gentle bend on the back straight, the first of two; flat out.
corners.9: Second gentle back-straight bend, flat out, the road falling toward the braking zone for the 90-degree 10A left.
corners.10A: Plain 90-degree left, marked by its curbs. Brake straight, easing pressure as you go deeper, then turn in near the end of the entry curb while trailing off the brake to keep the front loaded. At the apex, be as close to parallel with the apex curb as you can.
corners.10B: Second most important corner, as it opens onto the second-longest straight. A good 10A puts you on the left and already on throttle before you turn in. Apex late anyway to keep exit steering to a minimum.
corners.11: Slight blind right kink under the bridge, setting up T12. Apex is where the bridge ends, at the patch of grass sticking out on the right; choose a reference on the bridge to aim under and turn in toward a point just past its end.
corners.12: Fast downhill right, limited sight lines; it only feels manageable from the correct line. Come down the hill on that line, keep left to widen the entry, and turn in gradually at the end of the left entry curb. Stay off the apex and exit curbs, which upset the car.

notes.source: Written for Nestor from public corner guides: https://www.allenbergracingschools.com/expert-advice/road-atlanta-corner-by-corner/ (Allen Berg Racing Schools corner-by-corner guide, written for their Tatuus open-wheeler). Facts only; wording is our own.
